constraints_observed.web_access: public documentation only, read-only HTTP GET

claim_class_definitions.DOCUMENTED_FACT: Stated by a cited primary source (publisher repo at an exact commit, publisher licence text, technical report) or by a cited third-party page where labelled; includes values derived by trivial arithmetic only where marked.
claim_class_definitions.INDEPENDENTLY_REPRODUCED: Reproduced by this repository's own persisted evidence (file cited) or re-derived offline from such evidence.
claim_class_definitions.UNTESTED_HYPOTHESIS: Estimate, inference or judgment; never measured. Includes every memory/cost figure and rubric score.
claim_class_definitions.NOT_VERIFIED: Could not be verified in this pass (tool limitation, HTTP/empty result, source not read).

license_status_rules: GRANTED requires a retrieved licence text whose sha256 and git blob sha1 are stored and re-verifiable offline; ambiguity is never converted to GRANTED. GRANTED is a statement about the licence text only, not a selection.

retrieval_session.tool: Firecrawl scrape/search (read-only HTTP GET); no WebFetch summarisation used for any recorded fact
retrieval_session.direct_curl: Direct HTTPS to huggingface.co from the sandbox is policy-blocked (CONNECT 403); only www.apache.org was reachable by curl and was used for the canonical Apache-2.0 reference text.
tool_limitations: The Firecrawl rawHtml format strips angle-bracket tokens (<think>, <tools>, <s>) from text/plain files; the markdown format preserves them for JSON/text files. Recorded texts were therefore taken from the markdown format.

Tool output cannot be written to disk directly; each recorded text file was reconstructed by the agent and then mechanically verified against the Hugging Face git blob id (ETag / tree oid) of the file at the pinned commit. A text is stored only if its git blob sha1 equals the primary source's oid (byte-exact proof).

Firecrawl 'query' extraction (used for arXiv PDF tables, vLLM docs rows, ollama.com pages) is an LLM-based extraction by the tool; those facts are labelled extraction=tool_query and are never used for license, identity or hash claims.
Hugging Face reports lastModified at repository level; per-file commit dates were not retrieved.

claims.statement: HF Jinja template (3945 bytes, sha256 e4676cb56dffea7782fd3e2b577cfaf1e123537e6ef49b3ec7caa6c095c62272): '[INST]...[/INST]' format, system message prepended to the LAST user message, strict user/assistant alternation (raises otherwise), [AVAILABLE_TOOLS]/[TOOL_CALLS]/[TOOL_RESULTS] with 9-character tool-call ids, no thinking mode. This sha256 equals the repo-recorded hash of the cached pinned snapshot.

Repo root-cause analysis: under transformers 5.16.1 / tokenizers 0.23.2 AutoTokenizer on the pinned snapshot returns MistralCommonBackend (selected because tekken.json is present), which carries no chat_template -> vLLM 0.29.0 raises ChatTemplateResolutionError (HTTP 400) before generation; the same files without tekken.json resolve the template (sha256 e4676cb5...).
limitations: the container's own tokenizer class was not directly observed (repo states this)

claims.statement: generation_config.json contains only bos/eos ids (no sampling defaults). Model card: 'Unlike previous Mistral models, Mistral Nemo requires smaller temperatures. We recommend to use a temperature of 0.3'; examples use temperature 0.35.

Model card recommends mistral_inference / mistral_common; transformers usage needs a version supporting the model ('install from source' note); function calling requires 9-character alphanumeric tool-call ids. Ollama lists mistral-nemo:latest at 7.1GB.

estimate_formulas.nf4_effective_bytes_per_param: 0.5 + 1/64 + 4/(64*256) = 0.5159 (4-bit code + 8-bit absmax per 64 values + fp32 constant per 256 blocks, i.e. double quantization)
estimate_formulas.qlora_static: (P - E) x 0.5159 + E x 2, E = vocab x hidden x (1 if tied else 2) (embeddings/lm_head kept BF16)
estimate_formulas.lora_trainable: per layer r x [(h+q) + 2(h+kv) + (q+h) + 3(h+I)], q=heads x head_dim, kv=kv_heads x head_dim, h=hidden, I=intermediate; times layers (all linear layers)
estimate_formulas.lora_state: trainable x 16 B (fp32 weight 4 + grad 4 + AdamW m,v 8); paged 8-bit AdamW would be ~10 B
estimate_formulas.activations_ckpt: L x 2 x s x h (checkpointed layer inputs, BF16) + 34 x s x h (one recomputed layer, flash attention) + s x V x 6 (BF16 logits + FP32 upcast)
estimate_formulas.activations_no_ckpt: L x 34 x s x h + s x V x 6
estimate_formulas.peak: static + lora_state(r=16) + activations + 1.5 GB allocator/context overhead; band 0.8x-1.4x (the package's own band)
estimate_formulas.kv_cache_per_token: 2 x layers x kv_heads x head_dim x 2 B (BF16)
estimate_formulas.training_throughput: tokens/s = u x 989e12 / (6 P), u in [0.15, 0.25]; USD/1M tokens = 3.95/3600/tokens_per_s x 1e6
estimate_formulas.serving_throughput: step = (2P + B x ctx x kv/token) / (3.35e12 x 0.5); tokens/s = B/step; B=16, ctx=2048; USD/1M = 3.95/3600/tokens_per_s x 1e6 / utilisation

Primary sources confirm BOTH numbers and the model card explains the gap (40,960 = 32,768 output + 8,192 prompt reservation). harness_errors.title: Smoke prompts B and C do not instruct the output format that the acceptance expects
harness_errors.observed: B sends the bare user message '2 + 3' and requires content to equal exactly '5'; C sends 'Return valid JSON:\n{"status":"ready"}' and requires the whole content to parse as that object. Qwen3-8B answered '2 + 3 = 5' (correct); Phi-4 answered '2 + 3 equals 5.' and, for C, 'The JSON you provided is already valid. Here it is again for clarity: ...'; Nemo answered with a worked calculation and fenced JSON.
harness_errors.diagnosis: Contract/prompt mismatch: the prompt never says 'reply with only the number' (B) and C is ambiguous between 'validate this JSON' and 'emit this JSON'. Phi-4's reply to C is a reasonable reading of the prompt. The failures are measured against an acceptance the prompt does not request. The package already says these are response-format, not capability, failures.
harness_errors.proposed_fix_not_applied: Author a v2 locked protocol with explicit output-format instructions ('Reply with only the digit', 'Output only a JSON object') and re-pin; replay the persisted raw outputs through a semantic acceptance function (reevaluate-smokes mode exists) to report what each model would score under a tolerant policy, as a separate non-qualifying column.

harness_errors.title: Output-token budget differs per control and is outside the locked-protocol fingerprint
harness_errors.observed: smoke_max_tokens is 1024 for Qwen3-8B but 64 for Mistral-Nemo and Phi-4 (scripts/phase21b_4_20_control_runtime_qualification.py lines 79/87/94). Phi-4 smoke C ended with finish_reason='length' after exactly 64 completion tokens while Nemo's C (51 tokens) and Qwen's finished with 'stop'.
harness_errors.diagnosis: The locked protocol sha256 (d462103b...) covers prompts and acceptance only; max_tokens is a per-control config value. Phi-4's smoke C could not complete its reply, so the 'content is not valid JSON' verdict conflates a truncated answer with a wrong one; budgets are not equal across candidates.
harness_errors.proposed_fix_not_applied: Pin one max_tokens in the protocol; classify finish_reason='length' as INCONCLUSIVE_TRUNCATED (not MODEL_RUNTIME failure); add an offline unit test over the persisted raw responses.

harness_errors.title: Runtime qualification and behavioural contract are conflated in one acceptance gate
harness_errors.observed: RUNTIME_QUALIFIED requires every smoke to be exactly satisfied (compute_smoke_acceptance), so a server that loaded the pinned identity, answered HTTP 200 x3 with finish_reason=stop and clean cleanup is recorded runtime FAILED.
harness_errors.diagnosis: Verbosity of an instruct model is a behaviour property, not a serving defect (the package says so). Splitting the verdicts would let runtime compatibility (criterion E) be read from evidence without being contaminated by format behaviour (criteria F/G).
harness_errors.proposed_fix_not_applied: Report two independent columns - SERVING_OK (identity, BF16, HTTP 200, non-empty, finish_reason=stop, cleanup) and CONTRACT_COMPLIANCE (exact/semantic) - without changing the existing frozen records; derive them offline from persisted raw outputs.

harness_errors.title: Smoke A is streamed, B and C are not
harness_errors.observed: Locked protocol sets stream=true only for A. A passed for Qwen3 and Phi-4 and failed for Nemo with different transports than B/C.
harness_errors.diagnosis: Different request path (SSE assembly vs JSON body) between smokes confounds 'ready' vs 'instruction' behaviour; no evidence it changed an outcome, but it is an uncontrolled variable.
harness_errors.proposed_fix_not_applied: Add a CPU test that feeds the recorded raw A response through the SSE assembler and compares with a non-streaming replay in a mock; or run all smokes in both modes under a future authorization.

harness_errors.title: Mistral-Nemo: HF chat-template resolution fails because tekken.json flips AutoTokenizer to MistralCommonBackend
harness_errors.observed: Attempts 1-2: HTTP 400 'default chat template is no longer allowed ... provide a chat template'. Repo CPU analysis shows the pinned tokenizer_config.json does contain a 3,945-byte chat_template (sha256 e4676cb5...), but with tekken.json present transformers 5.16.1 returns MistralCommonBackend (no chat_template, get_chat_template raises); without tekken.json the template resolves and renders '<s>[INST]...[/INST]'.
harness_errors.diagnosis: Tooling interaction, established CPU-only by GENESIS_MISTRAL_NEMO_CHAT_TEMPLATE_ROOT_CAUSE_ANALYSIS_V2; the vLLM log line 'Detected the chat template content format to be string' is emitted even when no template resolved and is misleading.
harness_errors.proposed_fix_not_applied: Already addressed by candidate `mistral_nemo_native_v1` (--tokenizer-mode mistral, executed once as attempt 3). Offline alternatives for future work: stage a snapshot variant without tekken.json (changes the pinned file set and its hash manifest) or add a CPU preflight asserting 'tokenizer.chat_template is not None' before any GPU launch.

harness_errors.title: Greedy decoding is implicit: vLLM applies the model's generation_config.json defaults for fields the request omits
harness_errors.observed: Repo raw log (Qwen3 attempt 5, line 78): 'Default vLLM sampling parameters have been overridden by the model's generation_config.json: {temperature: 0.6, top_k: 20, top_p: 0.95}'. The locked request sends temperature, top_p, seed and max_tokens only.
harness_errors.diagnosis: For Qwen3 the leftover top_k=20 is harmless under temperature 0. For Qwen2.5-3B (repetition_penalty 1.05 in generation_config) and any model with penalties, a temperature-0 request is not guaranteed to be plain argmax unless the server is started with --generation-config vllm or the request sets every sampling field (UNTESTED_HYPOTHESIS for Qwen2.5-3B; the vLLM behaviour itself is shown in the repo log).
harness_errors.proposed_fix_not_applied: Record the effective sampling parameters in every evidence record (parse the vLLM startup warning) and add --generation-config vllm (or explicit top_k=-1, repetition_penalty=1.0) to a future protocol revision.

harness_errors.title: Qwen3 attempt 4 judged TECHNICAL_SUCCESS then reclassified; attempt-5 record carried a stale reasoning_mode

harness_errors.diagnosis: Acceptance and metadata were derived from capability defaults rather than the effective request; fixed by deriving from the approved configuration.
harness_errors.proposed_fix_not_applied: Keep the validator rule that metadata must be derived from the effective configuration; add a test asserting reasoning_tokens==0 whenever enable_thinking=false is recorded.

harness_errors.diagnosis: Billing-logic defects (not model issues), fixed by object-id attribution, the aged-out-app rule and adjustment reconciliation. Zero owner cash was billed in the control program after the GLM incident (3.52 USD owner-billed in the earlier 21B.4.13 GLM run).
